subject: Packaging, upgrade paths, and bundling options for AcmeApps
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@acmeapps.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:03:00 -0000
Subject: Packaging options and upgrade path

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency and the model routing features. We're starting to map internal teams to a Redwood plan but I need clarity on three things before I share with procurement: 

1) If we start on Standard with 50k tokens/month and later upgrade to Enterprise, how is the transition billed? Any proration or credit for unused months?
2) Are feature bundles (e.g., Advanced Observability + KV caching tier) only available on Enterprise or can they be add-ons to lower tiers?
3) What's the discount cadence for commitment levels (12 vs 24 vs 36 months)? We have a fairly predictable token profile and want to model TCO.

Attached is our high-level RFP (Acme_Redesign_RFP.pdf). Can you put together a recommendation and ballpark pricing we can show procurement?

Cheers,
Samir
Head of Platform
AcmeApps

---
Attachment: Acme_Redesign_RFP.pdf (application/pdf, 480KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@acmeapps.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options and upgrade path

Hi Samir — great to hear the demo resonated. Short answers up front, I'll follow with a concise quote: 

1) Upgrades: proration applies to committed capacity. If you upgrade mid-term we credit unused reservation toward the new tier for the remainder of the billing period; for metered (pay-as-you-go) we bill the delta on a pro-rata basis.
2) Bundles: Some advanced features are Enterprise-only (e.g., Private VPC control plane, extended observability retention), but many Optimize features (KV caching config, suggested batching profiles) can be added to Standard as a paid add-on.
3) Discounts: Typical progression is 10% (12m), 15% (24m), 18-20% (36m) on committed spend for hosted inference; we can be more competitive for multi-product deals or if you commit to Dedicated pools.

Marcus and Neha — looping you in for precise list of add-on SKUs and formal quote. I'll put together a multipath recommendation (Start+Add-ons -> Dedicated reserved -> Private) with pricing ranges by EOD tomorrow.

Next steps for Samir: can you confirm the token profile by workload (chat vs embeddings vs reranking) and whether data residency (EU workloads) is a factor? That'll affect whether we recommend Dedicated or hosted+burst.

Best,
Kimberly
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimmie@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging - draft pricing table and upgrade examples

Kim — I drafted a compact pricing table and a couple of upgrade/downgrade scenarios. Attaching the workbook (Redwood-pricing-quote-v3.xlsx). Key points: 

- 12/24/36m guidance for hosted Standard (50k tokens/mo baseline): 12m = 10% off list, 24m = 15%, 36m = 19%
- Observable add-on: $750/mo for 50k baseline; scales with committed tokens (50k increments)
- Enterprise base includes Private VPC options, extended retention; Dedicated pricing quoted separately
- Upgrade example: Customer on Standard 50k -> upgrade to Enterprise mid-term (month 8 of 12): we credit remaining 4 months of the Standard reserved portion; customer pays difference between new committed price and remaining credit pro-rated. No backdating.
- Downgrade policy: Downgrades can only take place at renewal unless there's a material change in usage; otherwise the committed price applies for the remainder of commitment.

Neha — can you validate the wording on the downgrade policy and confirm we can offer a 1.5% prepay credit for 36m if they prepay up front?

Laura — FYI for legal redlines on enterprise feature entitlements.

-Marcus

Subject: Re: Packaging - downgrade wording and prepay credit

Quick note on downgrade language and prepay: 

- Downgrade: confirm as Marcus wrote — downgrades effective at renewal only. For Enterprise accounts where the customer moves to a lower tier due to business reasons we will allow a one-time exception with a 60-day notice and a small administrative fee equal to 2% of remaining commitment. We should include that exception text in the SOW if needed.
- Prepay credit: legal plus finance sign off on 1.5% net price credit for full 36m prepay. Do not promise higher without finance approval.

Also recommend we include a short appendix in the quote that maps feature bundles to SKU codes (helps procurement).

-Neha

Hi Samir / Procurement — attaching a concise two-page quote that shows the three commitment horizons and both paths we discussed:

Path A — Start on Standard + Observability add-on (fast to provision):
- 12m: list $12,000/mo, net w/10% = $10,800/mo
- 24m: list $12,000/mo, net w/15% = $10,200/mo
- 36m: list $12,000/mo, net w/19% = $9,720/mo (1.5% prepay credit if they pay up front)
- Observability add-on: $750/mo at 50k baseline (scales)
- Upgrade: proration credit applied to reserved portion; downgrades at renewal only (exception available with 60-day notice + 2% admin fee)

Path B — Enterprise (includes advanced features + SSO, extended retention):
- 12m list $20,000/mo, net ~18,000/mo (10%)
- 24m net ~17,000/mo (15%)
- 36m net ~16,200/mo (19% + 1.5% prepay if applicable)

I've attached Redwood-pricing-quote-v3.xlsx and a short appendix that maps feature bundles to SKUs. If you want a Dedicated pool instead of hosted we can provide a separate committed capacity quote (different headroom math).

Next steps: 
- Samir: confirm target horizon and whether you want to start on Standard+add-ons or request Enterprise SOW.
- Procurement: if you want a formal contract/PO-ready quote I can route this to legal and generate a DocuSign link.

I'll leave Marcus and Neha on for any follow-up pricing/legal questions.

Thanks,
Kimberly
